body.statement:
For every fixed known \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\), every \(n\ge2\), and every parameter tuple satisfying \(S\le S_\star\), there are two finite priors \(\Pi_+,\Pi_-\) on \(\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) with constant target values separated by at least \(c\rho_n\), whose genuine fixed-\(n\) observed-data mixtures satisfy
\[
H^2\!\left(\int P_O^{\otimes n}\,d\Pi_+,\int P_O^{\otimes n}\,d\Pi_-\right)\le\frac14.
\]
The conditional sign mixtures agree on singleton components, every component of size \(r\ge2\) obeys
\[
H^2(Q_{r,+},Q_{r,-})\le Ca^2b^2r^4(9/2)^r,
\]
and the full squared Hellinger distance is at most \(Cn^2h^d\ell^da^2b^2\).  The priors retain exact uniform covariate support and require neither Poissonization nor an occupancy event.
body.proof_tex:
We construct the priors directly for the fixed point \(x_0\) and the fixed sample size \(n\).  Let \(D=[0,1]^d\), \(p=3/8\), and choose a nonnegative \(C^\infty\) function \(k:\mathbb R^d\to[0,1]\), supported on \([-1,1]^d\), with \(k(0)=1\).  For example, normalize the product of \(e^{-1/(1-t^2)}\mathbf1\{|t|<1\}\) in the coordinates.  Put
\[
 k_{x_0,h}(x)=k\!\left(\frac{\sigma\odot(x-x_0)}h\right),
 \qquad K_{x_0,h}(x)=k_{x_0,h}(x)^2,                                \tag{19}
\]
where \(\sigma_k=1\) if \(x_{0k}\le1/2\) and \(\sigma_k=-1\) otherwise.  Symmetry of the support makes the sign immaterial to its size, but the orientation identifies an inward face at a boundary point.  The restriction of (19) to \(D\) is smooth, equals one at \(x_0\), and has active volume at most \((2h)^d\); truncation by the boundary only decreases that volume.  Thus boundary points require no extension of the design support.

At scale \(\ell\), put
\[
 J_\ell=\{j\in\mathbb Z^d:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\ell j,D)\le\ell\},\qquad
 \phi_j(x)=\prod_{k=1}^d e^{-1/(1-(x_k/\ell-j_k)^2)}
                    \mathbf1\{|x_k/\ell-j_k|<1\},
\]
\[
 A_\ell(x)=\sum_{j\in J_\ell}\phi_j(x)^2,\qquad
 \psi_j(x)=\phi_j(x)A_\ell(x)^{-1/2}.
\]
The set \(J_\ell\) is finite.  Nearest-integer rounding gives an active translate within distance \(1/2\) in every coordinate, so \(A_\ell\) is bounded below by a positive constant on a neighborhood of \(D\).  The quotient rule and scaling therefore give
\[
 \sum_j\psi_j(x)^2=1,\quad
 \operatorname{supp}(\psi_j)\subseteq\{x:\|x-\ell j\|_\infty\le\ell\},\quad
 \|D^\nu\psi_j\|_\infty\le C_\nu\ell^{-|\nu|},                  \tag{20}
\]
and at most \(3^d\) functions are active at one point.

For independent Rademacher signs \(\vartheta_j\), define
\[
 F_\vartheta(x)=k_{x_0,h}(x)\sum_j\vartheta_j\psi_j(x),\qquad K(x)=K_{x_0,h}(x). \tag{21}
\]
Then, with \(B=3^{d/2}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_\vartheta F_\vartheta=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_\vartheta F_\vartheta^2=K,\qquad
 |F_\vartheta|\le B.                                                \tag{22}
\]
The product rule, (20), and \(\ell\le h\) show for every fixed \(s>0\) that
\[
 \|F_\vartheta\|_{\mathcal H_d^s(1)}\le C_s\ell^{-s},\qquad
 \|K\|_{\mathcal H_d^s(1)}\le C_sh^{-s}.                           \tag{23}
\]
For the fractional seminorm in (23), an order-\(m=\lceil s\rceil-1\) derivative is bounded both by \(Cr^{-m}\) and, by the mean-value theorem, by \(Cr^{-m-1}\|x-y\|_\infty\); splitting at \(\|x-y\|_\infty=r\) gives \(Cr^{-s}\|x-y\|_\infty^{s-m}\), including the integral case \(s-m=1\).

For \(\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 e_\vartheta&=p+aF_\vartheta,\\
 \mu_{0,\varepsilon,\vartheta}&=\frac12+\varepsilon bF_\vartheta
       +\frac{\varepsilon ab}{1-p}K,\\
 \tau_\varepsilon&=-\frac{\varepsilon ab}{p(1-p)}K,\\
 \mu_{1,\varepsilon,\vartheta}&=\frac12+\varepsilon bF_\vartheta
       -\frac{\varepsilon ab}{p}K.                                  \tag{24}
\end{aligned}
\]
Choose
\[
 \ell=c_\ell n^{-\eta/S},\qquad h=\ell^{S/\gamma},\qquad
 a=c_a\ell^\alpha,\qquad b=c_b\ell^\beta.                           \tag{25}
\]
Because \(S\le S_\star<\gamma\), \(0<\ell\le h\le1\).  Equations (23)--(25) give
\[
 a\ell^{-\alpha}=c_a,\quad b\ell^{-\beta}=c_b,\quad
 ab h^{-\gamma}=c_ac_b,\quad
 ab h^{-\beta}=c_ac_b\ell^{S(1-\beta/\gamma)}\le c_ac_b.             \tag{26}
\]
Starting from the constants \(4p=3/2\) and \(1/2\), choose the positive constants \(c_a,c_b\) sufficiently small, depending only on the fixed parameters.  The defining derivative and seminorm bounds in (23), (26), and \(L\ge4\) then prove
\[
 4e_\vartheta\in\mathcal H_d^\alpha(L),\quad 1\le4e_\vartheta\le2,\quad
 \mu_{0,\varepsilon,\vartheta}\in\mathcal H_d^\beta(L),\quad
 \tau_\varepsilon\in\mathcal H_d^\gamma(L),\quad
 \frac18\le\mu_{a,\varepsilon,\vartheta}\le\frac78.                \tag{27}
\]
For each \((\varepsilon,\vartheta)\), draw \(X\) exactly uniformly on \(D\), draw \(A\mid X=x\) as Bernoulli \(e_\vartheta(x)\), draw the two potential outcomes conditionally independently with the means in (24), independently of \(A\) given \(X\), and set \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).  Thus consistency and conditional exchangeability hold by construction, the response law is Bernoulli, and (27) proves membership in \(\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\).  Let \(\Pi_\varepsilon\) be uniform over the finite sign vectors.  Since \(K(x_0)=1\), its target is constant and
\[
 |\tau_+(x_0)-\tau_-(x_0)|=\frac{2ab}{p(1-p)}.                       \tag{28}
\]

We next prove the mixture bound for the actual fixed-\(n\) product experiment.  At a fixed \(x\), replace \((a,\varepsilon b)\) by real variables \((s,t)\) in (24).  In the four cells \((A,Y)=(1,1),(1,0),(0,1),(0,0)\), direct multiplication gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
q_{11}&=p/2+sF/2+ptF+st(F^2-K)-s^2tKF/p,\\
q_{10}&=p/2+sF/2-ptF-st(F^2-K)+s^2tKF/p,\\
q_{01}&=(1-p)/2-sF/2+(1-p)tF-st(F^2-K)-s^2tKF/(1-p),\\
q_{00}&=(1-p)/2-sF/2-(1-p)tF+st(F^2-K)+s^2tKF/(1-p).                 \tag{29}
\end{aligned}
\]
Using (22) in (29) shows that the sign average of each cell is the corresponding coordinate of
\(q_0=(p/2,p/2,(1-p)/2,(1-p)/2)\), independently of the sign of \(t\).  Thus every singleton component agrees exactly; there is no singleton leakage.

After decreasing \(c_a,c_b\), all ratios \(q_z/q_{0,z}\) lie in \([1/2,3/2]\), and their first \(s\), first \(t\), and mixed derivatives are bounded by a constant.  For fixed locations \(x_1,\ldots,x_r\), let
\[
 M_r(s,t;z_{1:r})=\mathbb E_\vartheta\prod_{i=1}^r
 \frac{q_{z_i}(s,t;x_i)}{q_{0,z_i}}.
\]
The product rule has \(r\) terms with both derivatives on one factor and \(r(r-1)\) with derivatives on distinct factors, whence
\[
 |\partial_s\partial_tM_r(s,t;z_{1:r})|\le Cr^2(3/2)^r.              \tag{30}
\]
At \(s=0\), the transformation \(\vartheta\mapsto-\vartheta\) shows \(M_r(0,b)=M_r(0,-b)\).  Twice applying the fundamental theorem of calculus to (30), and using \(M_r\ge2^{-r}\), gives
\[
 H^2(Q_{r,+},Q_{r,-})\le Ca^2b^2r^4(9/2)^r,\qquad r\ge2.             \tag{31}
\]

Condition on the realized \(X_{1:n}\).  Retain observations in the support of \(k_{x_0,h}\), and connect \(i,j\) when \(\|X_i-X_j\|_\infty\le2\ell\).  By (20), different connected components use disjoint sign coordinates, so the conditional mixture factors over components.  Product Hellinger affinities and \(1-\prod_j u_j\le\sum_j(1-u_j)\) imply that the conditional squared Hellinger distance is at most the sum of (31).  If \(N_r\) is the number of size-\(r\) components, a connected labeled set contains a spanning tree.  Deleting the least labeled leaf successively records a word of length \(r-2\) over the \(r\) labels; the reverse procedure, which adjoins the least label absent from the remaining word, reconstructs the unique tree.  This bijection gives exactly \(r^{r-2}\) labeled trees.  Sequential integration of a root and its children therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E N_r\le {n\choose r}r^{r-2}(2h)^d(4\ell)^{d(r-1)}.         \tag{32}
\]
Because \(r!\ge(r/e)^r\), (31)--(32) yield
\[
 \mathbb E_XH^2\{\mathsf M_+(\cdot\mid X_{1:n}),\mathsf M_-(\cdot\mid X_{1:n})\}
 \le Cn^2h^d\ell^da^2b^2                                          \tag{33}
\]
provided \(C_0n\ell^d\le1/2\); this follows by summing the resulting geometric series beginning at \(r=2\).  Both mixtures have the same uniform \(X_{1:n}\)-marginal, so integrating the conditional Hellinger affinity shows that (33) is exactly the unconditional fixed-\(n\) squared Hellinger bound.  No conditioning event and no Poissonization has been used.

Finally,
\[
 1-\frac{d\eta}{S}\le0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad S\le\frac{d\gamma}{2\gamma+d}=S_\star. \tag{34}
\]
Hence \(n\ell^d\le c_\ell^d\); at equality it is exactly \(c_\ell^d\), so choosing \(c_\ell\) small proves the series condition rather than producing a logarithm.  Moreover,
\[
 n^2h^d\ell^da^2b^2
 =c_a^2c_b^2 n^2\ell^{2S+d+Sd/\gamma}=C(c_a,c_b,c_\ell),             \tag{35}
\]
because \(\eta(2+d/S+d/\gamma)=2\).  Decreasing \(c_\ell>0\) makes (33) at most \(1/4\), while (28) becomes
\[
 |\tau_+(x_0)-\tau_-(x_0)|
 =\frac{2c_ac_bc_\ell^S}{p(1-p)}n^{-\eta}=c\rho_n.                  \tag{36}
\]
All constants are positive and depend only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), uniformly over \(x_0\).  This proves every asserted support, separation, component, and fixed-product property.
